This work aimed to (i) characterize the physicochemical quality of groundwater from fifteen sampling points, comprising seven boreholes (F1-F7) and eight wells (P1-P8), and (ii) evaluate its suitability for domestic use against World Health Organization guideline values (WHO, 2022). posts.title: Permafrost Detachment Slides: A Distinct High‐Magnitude Permafrost Mass Wasting Process
posts.abstract_original: Abstract Warming permafrost is destabilizing landscapes, intensifying thaw‐driven mass wasting and giving rise to novel landslide forms. We characterize two recent (2017 and 2018), deep‐seated translational failures that we term Permafrost Detachment Slides (PDSs), which rapidly translocated 4.5 and 18 × 10 6 m 3 of frozen material into downstream environments. The PDS failure mechanism involves bottom‐up thaw, initiating gradual movement of the entire permafrost layer, producing distinct failure styles and deposits. Initial movement results in extensional cracks that increase water infiltration, accelerating thaw at depth and slope failure.

posts.abstract_original: ABSTRACT Central Australia's ngarrawa, or ‘mound springs’, are unique hydrological systems that serve as some of the only near‐permanent sources of water and continuous sediment deposition in Australia's arid interior. As such, they hold significant potential as palaeo‐climate and ‐environmental archives in a region where many aspects of past climate remain uncertain. To date, few studies have investigated the potential of these sediments, including their stratigraphic integrity or if they can be radiocarbon‐dated. posts.title: Assessing the positioning accuracy of channel extracted from DEM: a test of channel offset
posts.abstract_original: River network extraction from DEMs is crucial for hydrological analysis. While the accuracy of watershed area and river length have been widely tested, spatial positioning accuracy lacks attention. posts.title: Soil and Water Assessment Tool reveals dominant baseflow in semi-arid catchment with sand dams in Kenya
posts.abstract_original: Introduction Increasing water scarcity and climate variability threaten rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions. Sand dams are widely used as Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to retain water within the sandy matrix of ephemeral riverbeds, yet their catchment-scale hydrological effects remain insufficiently quantified. Methods We applied the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT+) in a 22.35 km 2 ungauged ephemeral catchment in Makueni County, Kenya, containing 22 sand dams. posts.title: Scenario-driven optimization of land-use/land-cover conversion pathways to improve ecosystem service performance in the Yellow River Basin
posts.abstract_original: Future land use/land cover (LULC) conversions provide a critical pathway for improving ecosystem service (ES) outcomes in large river basins, yet their contributions to comprehensive ES performance and functional synergies remain insufficiently quantified. This study projected the future dynamics of five representative ES metrics: carbon storage (CS), water yield (WY), nutrient export (NE), soil conservation (SC), and habitat quality (HQ) across multiple spatiotemporal scales in the Yellow River Basin, China. posts.title: Petrophysical Joint Inversion of Electrical and Seismic Tomographic Data Including Shear Waves
posts.abstract_original: Summary Petrophysical characterization in near-surface environments remains challenging due to the high heterogeneity, sharp contrasts in fluid content, and complex hydrogeological structures. This work introduces a novel petrophysical joint inversion (PJI) framework that integrates SH-wave seismic refraction tomography (SRT) with electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) and, optionally, time-domain induced polarization (IP) data, replacing the conventional approach based on P-wave velocity and Wyllie’s equation with the Castagna relation for S-wave velocity. posts.title: Mineral-Organic Interactions and Soil Gradients Drive Plant Community Assembly in Brazilian Semiarid Inselbergs
authors: José João Lelis Leal de Souza
posts.abstract_original: This study investigated a soil catena along a colluvial slope of a southeast-facing granitic inselberg to evaluate the influence of soil property variations on vegetation composition across altitudinal and distance gradients from the inselberg. Four soil profiles were described and sampled along a toposequence. Soil analyses included texture, acidity, exchangeable bases, phosphorus, nitrogen, and organic carbon contents. Total porosity, macroporosity, and microporosity were determined using undisturbed soil samples. posts.title: Integrated geophysical and hydrogeochemical characterization of a fractured limestone aquifer in new Tuna El Gabel village, West El-Minia, Egypt
posts.abstract_original: Abstract Groundwater is a vital component of water supply in arid regions, such as West El-Minia Governorate, Egypt, where water scarcity is projected to worsen, with per capita water supply expected to drop below 500 m 3 by 2025. In response, Egypt’s One and a Half Million Feddan (≈630,000 hectares) project aims to reclaim the Western Desert and develop new communities, aligning with the country’s Vision 2030 for sustainable development. This study conducts a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative assessment of groundwater resources in the region, evaluating their suitability for various applications. posts.title: Hydrogeological characterization of fractured basement aquifers using an integrated analysis in the Agnéby-Tiassa region of southern Côte d’Ivoire
posts.abstract_original: Access to safe drinking water in the Agnéby-Tiassa region (southern Côte d’Ivoire) faces major challenges due to the inadequacy of surface water resources and a poor understanding of the potential of basement aquifers, which are often obscured by a thick regolith mantle and dense vegetation. This study proposes an integrated methodological approach aimed at a detailed characterization of the hydrogeological potential of these fractured formations to optimise the siting of high-yield boreholes. posts.title: From order to species: Modelling Amphipoda distributions in the Hamersley Range
posts.abstract_original: Groundwater amphipods in the Pilbara region of Western Australia are under pressure from the impacts of mining operations, particularly from groundwater extraction. To help inform conservation planning for this subterranean group, we model their distribution using a suite of environmental variables and occurrence data, and a Random Forest (RF) classification method. posts.title: Forecasting Marsh Resilience in the Plum Island Estuary: Integrating Uncertainty to Inform Coastal Management
posts.abstract_original: Abstract Salt marshes provide critical ecosystem services yet face increasing threats from accelerated relative sea-level rise (SLR). The long-term persistence of these habitats depends on their ability to vertically accrete and laterally migrate into adjacent uplands. Predicting the location and viability of these future marsh corridors is therefore a primary challenge for coastal managers; one often hindered by uncertainties in future water levels and topographic data accuracy, particularly in vegetated wetlands where light detection and ranging (lidar) data systematically overestimate elevation. posts.title: Exploring spatial variability in the physical and chemical properties of urban soils using electrical resistivity tomography
posts.abstract_original: Urban soils exhibit complex spatial heterogeneity resulting from the superposition of natural pedogenetic processes and variable anthropogenic disturbances. To optimize land-use planning and avoid inappropriate uses, it is essential to accurately characterize the spatial variability of soil properties and potential contamination. Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT), a geophysical method developed over several decades, is well suited to describe soil variability in highly heterogeneous, human-disturbed environments. posts.title: Charting the evolution of ecohydraulics: a community perspective on skills, technology, training needs and challenges
posts.abstract_original: Ecohydraulics requires the integration of diverse skill sets to understand the complex interactions among hydraulic, biological, and ecological processes in aquatic environments, particularly under the influence of natural and anthropogenic change. This article presents findings from a community survey conducted at the 15th International Symposium on Ecohydraulics and Fish Passage (ISE-FP 2024) and compares them to those of a similar survey conducted at ISE 2018, with a particular focus on early-career researchers. posts.title: Characterization and stability assessment of rare earth tailings under dry and paste stacking conditions
posts.abstract_original: The management of rare earth element (REE) tailings presents unique challenges due to their fine-grained nature, carbonate-rich composition, and potential environmental sensitivity. As Europe develops new carbonatite and phosphate-hosted REE projects, large volumes of tailings will require safe and sustainable storage. This study integrates physicochemical characterization, triaxial testing, particle breakage analysis, and numerical modelling to evaluate the behaviour of REE tailings within a tailings storage facility. posts.title: Velocity changes in the Haichenghe fault zone in Liaoning, China revealed by S-coda of repeating microearthquakes
posts.abstract: Abstract Monitoring temporal seismic velocity changes within active fault zones provides critical insights into crustal stress evolution and earthquake nucleation processes. Leveraging high-density observational data from the Liaoning Seismic Network and the Haicheng Dense Array, we identified 37 repeating sequences (comprising 89 events) and applied coda wave interferometry (CWI) to measure relative seismic velocity changes within the fault zone. posts.title: Temporal change in mass eruption rate estimated from co-eruptive seismograms during 2014–2018 eruption at Sinabung Volcano, Indonesia
posts.abstract_original: Abstract An effusive eruption occurred at Sinabung volcano, Indonesia, from December 2013 to February 2018. The eruption peaked with violent pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) and a lava flow in the first three months of 2014 and then gradually declined. After the lava flow activity ceased, in October 2014, minor PDCs repeated and Vulcanian eruptions started in August 2015. posts.title: Regional 3-D electrical resistivity model of Mongolia: Constraining lithospheric properties and architecture
posts.abstract_original: Sumamry Electrical resistivity models derived from magnetotelluric (MT) measurements across the Khangai Dome, an intracontinental plateau in central Mongolia, have identified several intriguing features, including a locally thinned lithosphere and extended fluid-rich domains in the lower crust. However, due to the limited spatial coverage of these studies, whether those features extend beyond central Mongolia could not be assessed. posts.title: Radiometric and geochemical indicators in anthills as guides for mineral exploration in Bashar Upper Benue Trough North Central Nigeria
posts.abstract_original: This study evaluates the potential of anthill radiometric and geochemical signatures as indicators for preliminary mineral exploration in the Bashar area of the Upper Benue Trough, north-central Nigeria. The objective was to assess the distribution of uranium (U), thorium (Th), and potassium (K) in anthill materials and evaluate their geological and exploration significance. posts.title: Integrated hydrogeochemical and microbiological assessment of groundwater quality in a fractured volcanic aquifer, Ibb City, Yemen
posts.abstract_original: Abstract Groundwater quality assessment in fractured volcanic aquifers presents significant challenges due to structural heterogeneity that may influence groundwater flow and contaminant transport. This study presents an integrated hydrogeochemical and microbiological assessment of groundwater from twenty production wells tapping the fractured volcanic aquifer of the Tertiary Yemen Volcanic Group in Ibb City, Yemen. Groundwater samples were collected during the dry season (November–December 2025). posts.title: Genesis of Alluvial Titanium Resources in the Bularafa Area of Yobe State: An Integrated Spatial and Petrographic Studies
posts.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE
posts.abstract_original: This study investigates the origin of an alluvial titanium resources located within the Bularafa Area of Yobe State. Thorough aeromagnetic map studies, comprehensive field mapping and petrographic examination, were employed to interpret the regional lithological framework and the processes controlling titanium mineralization. Spatial observations revealed that sedimentary units were intruded by distinct volcanic plugs exhibiting diverse structural features, including columnar jointing (vertical, dipping, and horizontal), brecciation, and layering. posts.title: Fluid and metal provenance of the Kiskamavaara Cu-Co deposit, northern Norrbotten, Sweden
posts.abstract_original: Abstract Kiskamavaara is a shear zone-hosted cobaltian pyrite and chalcopyrite deposit in Northern Norrbotten, Sweden. Although previously classified as an Iron Oxide Copper-Gold (IOCG) deposit, the dominance of pyrite is atypical, suggesting either an unusual IOCG variant or a deposit type with overlapping characteristics. Understanding deposits like Kiskamavaara, for which limited documentation exists, is critical for refining genetic models and regional exploration strategies. posts.title: Estimation of NATM excavation-support classes at tunnel excavation faces using a deep learning algorithm
posts.abstract_original: Accurate determination of the geotechnical conditions at the tunnel face is essential for ensuring safe and effective excavation and support operations during tunnel construction with New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM). Therefore, engineering geologists carefully and systematically collect geotechnical data from the excavation face to ensure reliable NATM excavation-support classes. posts.title: A study on the coupling of Rural-Land Use transformation and development in the karst mountains of southwest China: the case of Guizhou province
posts.abstract: Revealing the coupling coordination mechanism between rural transformation and land-use transformation in ecologically fragile regions is of theoretical and practical significance for addressing the paradox between ecological conservation and rural development, and for promoting sustainable development in karst mountainous areas. Drawing on social-ecological systems theory, this study develops an analytical framework for coupling Rural-Land Use transformation. posts.title: Electric Activity of Volcanic Clouds and Formation of Local Electric Field in Kamchatka
posts.abstract_original: The paper summarizes the contribution of Firstov P.P. to experimental studies of the vertical component of the atmospheric electric field (AEF Ez) at Paratunka Observatory (2006–2018). Based on the analysis of 47 publications and a monograph (Cherneva and Firstov, 2018), the key role of seasonal radon outflow in the formation of Ez variations is demonstrated. posts.title: The Role of Tectonic Inheritance in Active Rift Seismicity and Magmatism: Constraints From 3‐D Gravity Inversion and D‐InSAR Modeling of the 2025 Fentale Swarm, Ethiopia
posts.abstract_original: Abstract The role of inherited lithospheric structures in active rift seismicity and magma intrusion remains a key uncertainty in continental breakup dynamics. We investigate the January 2025 Northern Main Ethiopian Rift swarm using constrained 3‐D gravity inversion and D‐InSAR observations to characterize crustal architecture, seismicity, and active deformation. posts.title: Paleoseismic record on the Menshi segment of the Karakorum fault zone, southwestern Tibetan Plateau and its tectonic implications
posts.abstract_original: The Karakorum Fault Zone, a major dextral strike-slip structure extending over 1000 km along the western margin of the Tibetan Plateau, accommodates crustal deformation resulting from the ongoing India-Eurasia collision. Despite its high activity since the Late Quaternary, the recurrence behavior of large earthquakes on this fault system remains poorly constrained. The Menshi segment constitutes a structural transition zone characterized by complex geometry, featuring dominant southern and northern fault strands with intervening secondary branching faults. posts.title: Crustal Shear‐Wave Velocity and Azimuthal Anisotropy Imaging Reveals the Merapi‐Merbabu‐Telomoyo Volcanic Chain, Central Java
posts.abstract_original: Abstract We present new results from ambient noise tomography and azimuthal anisotropy analysis of the DOMERAPI data set to investigate crustal structure beneath the Merapi‐Merbabu‐Telomoyo region in central Java. posts.title: AI-powered, seismic hazard-integrated modeling of hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure in the Zagros Lurestan Provinces
posts.abstract_original: The increasing global demand for resilient subsurface energy systems requires understanding how active tectonics influence hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure behavior. Tectonically active regions, such as the Lurestan provinces of the Zagros Fold-Thrust Belt, pose persistent challenges due to structural complexity and pressure instability. posts.title: Modeling Long-Term Postseismic Deformation Following the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos Earthquake Using Campaign and Continuous GNSS Observations
posts.abstract_original: Postseismic deformation provides fundamental insights into earthquake-cycle processes, lithospheric rheology, and stress redistribution following large earthquakes. Although the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos earthquake has been extensively investigated in terms of coseismic deformation and early postseismic behavior, the long-term evolution of deformation following the event remains poorly constrained. posts.title: Joint inversion of seismic and geoelectrical data targeting geological faults
posts.abstract_original: Near-surface geological faults play a crucial role in subsurface systems because they influence fluid flow and transport and can cause geotechnical failure.
